tob-10086: This essay collection gathers Evelyn Underhill’s shorter writings on the nature of mysticism and the lives of individual mystics. The essays ask what mystical experience actually is, how it has been described across the centuries, and what it demands of those who seek it. Together they form a thoughtful introduction to her ideas beyond her better-known books.
tob-10486: John Edward Mercer’s study asks whether the wonder people feel before mountains, seas, and starry skies is itself a kind of religious experience. He surveys poets, saints, and scientists who found the divine in nature, from Wordsworth to the nature mystics of the Middle Ages. The book argues that reverence for the natural world belongs at the heart of spirituality.
tob-10786: H. Stanley Redgrove surveys alchemy’s long history — its Egyptian roots, its medieval masters, and its slow transformation into chemistry. He defends the alchemists as serious seekers after truth rather than mere charlatans, and examines their claims with a chemist’s eye. The book remains a balanced introduction to a much-mocked subject.
tob-4086: In this 1910 book Yeats sharpens his thrust at the Ireland of his day — its wire-pullers, its pieties, its sellouts. The title play-poem retells an old Irish tale with a modern sting. These are the poems of a man turning from myth to the rougher trade of public life.
tob-4286: Budge’s second Egypt-gods book bears on with the muster — deep studies in Egyptian wonder-tales, the great gods limned at large. His work stays the most readable door to the god-host. The pair together are a landmark of folk Egypt-lore.
arxiv-2605-08786: When a server farm or factory line fails, engineers must find the root cause hiding among hundreds of signals. Christopher Lohse, Anish Dhir, and Amadou Ba present PRIM, which meta-learns a Bayesian approach to root-cause analysis so it adapts quickly to failure types it has never seen. The 2026 paper is about diagnosing breakdowns faster, with uncertainty honestly measured.
arxiv-2605-08986: Quantum wires squeeze electrons into one dimension, and the ideal 1D electron gas trapped in an anisotropic wire has an exact solution — usually reached by the canonical route. E.I. Jafarov, S.M. Nagiyev, and J. Van der Jeugt work out what changes under the non-canonical approach. The 2026 paper is mathematical physics on exactly solvable quantum models.
arxiv-2605-09186: Mixed-integer programming solvers live or die by their constraint handlers — specialized code for each problem type. Liding Xu, Yugeng Zhou, and Sebastian Pokutta use AI agents to generate those handlers faster. The 2026 paper is agentic research applied to optimization itself.
arxiv-2605-09386: Zero-shot text-to-speech clones voices never heard in training, and scheduling the generation steps matters. Dong Yang, Yiyi Cai, Haoyu Zhang, and colleagues schedule kinetically optimally with moment correction for metric-induced discrete flow matching. The 2026 paper makes voice cloning faster and more faithful.
arxiv-2605-09486: Continuous-time quantum walks spread across graphs in ways classical walks cannot, and transformers can learn from the patterns. Zhan Li, Wuqing Yu, Yusen Wu, and Chuan Wang fuse the two in CTQWformer for graph classification. The 2026 paper is quantum-inspired graph learning.
arxiv-2605-09586: Jelly, cloth, dough — deformable objects are hard to model from video alone. Can Li, Zhoujian Li, Ren Li, and colleagues build DeformMaster: an interactive physics-neural world model learned from videos of squishy things. The 2026 paper teaches AI the physics of deformation.
arxiv-2605-10186: Legal language models must cite reliably — hallucinating cases is malpractice; LegalCiteBench evaluates citation reliability. Sijia Chen, Hang Yin, and Shunfan Zhou build the benchmark. The 2026 paper is legal AI evaluation. It checks every legal citation with true rigor and care.
arxiv-2605-10486: Leveraged event-linked markets — manipulation, insider information, and the regulation that should tame them. Maksym Nechepurenko analyzes the market microstructure. The 2026 paper is financial economics. It exposes how insiders exploit leveraged event-linked markets for profit. Regulation must catch up.
pmc-13407886: Acute kidney injury in Japanese outpatients — its seasonal pattern described. Yuka Sakazaki, Yuki Kondo, Mizuki Okuma, and colleagues track incidence through the year. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is nephrology. It finds kidneys fail on a schedule. Seasonality in kidney injury.
pmc-13495586: Neuro-oncology organs-at-risk — delineated with multimodal deep learning guided by the EPTN international contouring atlas. Ana M Barragán-Montero, Margerie Huet-Dastarac, and colleagues train the models. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is radiation oncology AI. It teaches AI to outline what radiation must spare.
pmc-13461386: Myasthenia gravis in adults over 70 — treated with or without prednisolone, in a retrospective cohort. Kazuo Iwasa, Yutaka Furukawa, Hiroaki Yoshikawa, and colleagues compare the strategies. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is geriatric neurology. It asks whether elderly myasthenics need steroids. Steroids, questioned.
pmc-13444186: Korean guidelines for pediatric procedural sedation — the national standard. Hye-Mi Lee, Young Sung Kim, Eun-Hee Kim, and colleagues author them. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is pediatric sedation guidelines. It standardizes sedating Korean children. Korea’s sedation standard. Children, safely sedated.
pmc-13518786: Drought-resistant soil microbes — their resistance bought at the expense of soil carbon loss. Xuesen Pang, Chengjie Ren, Nianpeng He, and colleagues uncover the trade-off. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is soil microbiology. It shows dry survival spending the soil's carbon.
pmc-13505386: Mesoporous covalent organic framework architectures — synthesized under interfacial-energy direction. Jing Tang and Yusuke Yamauchi do the synthesis. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is COF materials. It directs interfaces to build porous crystals. Porous crystals, engineered. Mesopores, designed. Mesoporous COFs, designed by interfacial energy.
pmc-13449786: ACSCull — visibility-aware triangle elimination for skinned characters under an admissible camera set. Jos Timanta Tarigan develops the algorithm. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is computer graphics. It culls unseen triangles to speed rendering. Triangles eliminated. ACSCull works. Triangle culling, smart.
pmc-13404786: Residual exercise pulmonary hypertension after balloon pulmonary angioplasty — improved by long-term supervised cardiac rehabilitation in chronic thromboembolic patients. Yuya Suzuki, Yoshihisa Nakano, Katsuhiro Okazaki, and colleagues run the rehab. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is cardiac rehabilitation. It exercises away lingering pulmonary hypertension.
arxiv-2606-16986: In string theory, the geometry of extra dimensions can leave fingerprints called anomalies, and physicists study how they concentrate at sharp points of toric geometries, spaces built from cones. This paper localizes the anomaly polynomial in such settings, with a black hole sitting at the cone's tip. The result tightens the link between geometry and consistent quantum theories.
arxiv-2606-17086: Gautam Shah, Vinod Ashokan, and colleagues predict excitonic condensation in an asymmetric electron-hole biwire, two parallel quantum wires with mismatched carriers. Excitonic condensation is a collective quantum state where electron-hole pairs move as one, a cousin of superconductivity. The asymmetry turns out to help, suggesting new designs for ultra-low-power electronics.
arxiv-2606-17286: Jeba Sania, Marta Ziosi, and Fazl Barez trace how AI systems enable authoritarianism by design. From democracies to autocracies, the same tools for safety and efficiency become instruments of control. Presented as a conference paper, it maps the design choices that tilt AI toward oppression, and how to resist them.
arxiv-2606-17386: Zikang Xiong and colleagues teach end-to-end driving policies without expert demonstrations. TerraTransfer learns from raw experience across terrains instead of imitating human drivers. The approach promises autonomous driving that adapts to roads no expert ever showed it. Training uses reinforcement signals from real driving outcomes rather than human labels.
arxiv-2606-17686: G. L. Comer, Nils Andersson, and colleagues take an action-based approach to dissipative relativistic fluid systems. The variational principle tames viscosity and heat in Einstein's universe. The formalism serves neutron star mergers and cosmology. The framework handles the extreme conditions inside merging neutron stars.
arxiv-2606-17886: Mikhail Krasnov and colleagues study monotonic Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, both theoretically and empirically. Monotonicity, where more input means more output, is a prized property in finance and medicine. KANs build functions from learnable curves, and the monotonic variant keeps them trustworthy. The paper maps when monotonicity helps and what it costs.
arxiv-2606-18186: Lekan Molu develops Kolmogorov regression for robust diffusion policies. The regression technique hardens robot policies against the unexpected. Diffusion policies generate smooth actions, and robustness keeps them safe. The work serves robots that must not fail. The policies stay reliable even when sensors lie or the world shifts.
arxiv-2606-18486: Faruk Alpay and Barış Başaran render separoid information through rate-distortion reconstruction of convex apartness scenes. The information-theoretic framework compresses geometric scenes optimally. Their reconstruction balances fidelity against bitrate. It is compression theory for spatial data.
plos-pone-0003386: Menthol cools more than skin, these 2008 neuroscientists found. Beyond its familiar action on cold-sensing TRPM8 channels in nerves, menthol turned out to target the brain's A-type GABA receptors, the main calming switches of the central nervous system. The dual action helps explain menthol's broader sensory effects, from soothing mint flavor to altered nerve signaling.
plos-pone-0003486: Theorist Becca Asquith weighed HIV's escape gambit in this 2008 paper. When the virus mutates to dodge killer T cells, it may pay a fitness cost, and she calculated the selective advantage of those escape variants and their contribution to HLA-driven viral evolution. The math clarifies how much dodging immunity actually costs the virus.
plos-pone-0003586: Vaccine researchers tested a TB protein pair in this 2008 paper. The PE25/PPE41 complex of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, part of a large family of shape-shifting surface proteins, triggered stronger antibody and cellular responses together than alone. The co-operonic pair emerges as a candidate for TB vaccines that need to outsmart an evasive pathogen.
plos-pone-0003686: In 2008, Fredriksson, Tjäder, and Keller found ICU patients' muscles starving at the power-plant level. In septic patients, the mitochondria of skeletal muscle lost their normal dynamics, and the muscle's gene activity shifted with the failure. The work traces the wasting weakness of severe sepsis down to broken energy machinery.
plos-pone-0003786: Khorsand and Chance studied neurons juggling two message streams in this 2008 paper. The average input and its variability can change independently, giving neurons two channels of information. Their spiking models show how cells react when both channels shift at once.
plos-pone-0003886: A 2008 ecology paper warned that extinction risk climbs toward the equator. The Vamosis showed tropical species face escalating danger, deepening the puzzle of the latitudinal diversity gradient. The tropics hold the most species and are losing them fastest.
plos-pone-0003986: In 2008, Sharma, Hughes, and Murillo auditioned a new gauge for kids with HIV. Interleukin-7 receptor alpha on CD8 T cells was tested as a disease-status marker. The marker could complement viral load and CD4 counts in guiding treatment. A sharper readout would help doctors time therapy changes for infected children.
plos-pone-0004086: In 2008, Dyer and Vuong found bees doing mental math on shapes. Insect brains used image interpolation to recognize rotated objects. The tiny visual system filled in missing views of 3D shapes. The trick shows small brains solving hard vision problems.
plos-pone-0004186: In 2009, Wieten, Berlo, and ten Brink found calm riding on a cytokine. IL-10 proved essential for mycobacterial HSP70's taming of arthritis. The heat-shock protein's anti-inflammatory effect needed IL-10. The pathway suggests new arthritis therapies. The finding links bacterial stress proteins to immune peace.
plos-pone-0004286: In 2009, a German team split the Cre tool in two. Split-Cre reunion revealed matched activity of gene pairs in living mice. Only cells running both genes lit up. The tool sharpens conditional genetics. The method improves on single-promoter Cre systems.
plos-pone-0004386: In 2009, a team linked a cattle germ to diabetes. Special blood tests tied a cattle bacterium to type-1 diabetes. The hardy germ surfaced in diabetic patients. The link needs causal testing. The work opens a new lead on diabetes triggers today.
plos-pone-0004486: In 2009, Scott, VanWye, and McDonald stress-tested gene chips hard and long. A hard look at gene chips measured spread across people. The chips' trust score was tallied. The study guides gene study design today. The spread was truly wide.
plos-pone-0004586: In 2009, Ande, Moulik, and Mishra found two tiny protein tags talking shop daily. Sugar and phosphate tags on prohibitin were mapped. The tags influenced each other quite strongly. The finding has diabetes implications today. The ancient protein is conserved widely today.
plos-pone-0004686: In 2009, Lodeiro, Theodoropoulou, and Pardo mapped hunger-hormone signaling anew. c-Src regulated Akt signaling in response to ghrelin. The β-arrestin pathways split in two quite cleanly. The neat study maps cell signaling wiring. The target kinase is a serine/threonine type.
plos-pone-0004786: In 2009, Agrillo, Dadda, and Serena found fish counting anew here today. Use of number by fish was demonstrated. The smart fish discriminated quantities quite well. The study maps numerical cognition roots well today. The number abilities are rudimentary yet real still.
plos-pone-0357286: How often couples have sex affects how quickly they conceive — but by how much? Drawing on Norway’s huge mother, father and child cohort study, this paper links reported intercourse frequency to fecundability, the per-cycle chance of pregnancy. The findings give couples and fertility doctors realistic numbers on how timing and frequency move the odds.
plos-pone-0357886: Aging blood vessels and failing hearts may share a molecular driver: HMOX2. This paper traced HMOX2-driven crosstalk between vascular aging and heart failure using bioinformatics, explainable machine learning, and laboratory validation. The crosstalk names a therapeutic target sitting at the intersection of two major killers.
plos-pone-0356186: Transporting piglets stresses the young animals badly — hurting welfare and growth alike. This paper tested astragalus polysaccharides for alleviating transport stress in piglets. The herbal supplement reduced stress markers, offering farmers a natural way to ease the journey for their animals.
plos-pone-0357586: Indigenous communities in Canada’s Northwest Territories face distinct barriers to HPV awareness. This study measured human papillomavirus and HPV vaccine awareness in these communities. The findings guide culturally safe outreach that respects Indigenous knowledge and leadership.
plos-pone-0356886: The slime coating yogurt bacteria — exopolysaccharide — may fight norovirus. This paper showed Lactobacillus delbrueckii-derived exopolysaccharide suppresses murine norovirus replication by modulating the innate immune response. The food-grade compound is an unexpected antiviral lead hiding in fermented milk.
plos-pone-0356686: Adolescents living with HIV in Kampala need HPV vaccination — and weren’t getting it. This pilot quality improvement project strengthened HPV vaccination among these adolescents in metropolitan Uganda. The project’s methods show other clinics exactly how to close the gap.
plos-pone-0357086: Long-term care facilities desperately need nurses — but do nursing students want those jobs? This qualitative study explored nursing undergraduates’ willingness to work in long-term care. Their candid views reveal what attracts — and repels — the next generation from elder care.
plos-pone-0357186: Artificial intelligence is reshaping microsurgery — and its trajectory can be forecast. This dual-component framework analyzed global publication trends to forecast AI-assisted microsurgery’s future. The trend analysis maps where the field is heading, helping surgeons and funders prepare.
plos-pone-0356486: Judging fluid volume status in hypernatremic — dangerously dehydrated — patients is notoriously tricky. This paper tested the clinical value of the caval–aortic index and inferior vena cava diameter for volume assessment. The ultrasound indices give clinicians objective numbers for fluid decisions.
plos-pone-0356786: Measuring how amputees walk shouldn’t require a million-dollar gait lab. This paper assessed IMU-derived lower-limb kinematics in transtibial amputees through a practical, accessible clinical workflow. The validated workflow brings quantitative gait analysis to ordinary clinics.
plos-pone-0342286: Prediction models that discriminate beautifully can still deceive — through separation-like irregularity and sample size optimism. This paper dissected both phenomena in high-discrimination logistic models. The statistical cautions protect researchers from mistaking overfitted brilliance for genuine predictive power.
plos-pone-0346386: ‘The hypothesis becomes forced’ — cultural narratives about deductive hypothesis testing shape how scientists see themselves. This paper showed these narratives influence scientists’ self-perception and actions. The findings suggest the textbook story of ‘the scientific method’ may be warping the very science it claims to describe.
plos-pone-0356286: Some patients survive invasive group A streptococcal disease only to die later — delayed mortality with mysterious biology. This paper profiled the transcriptome of that delayed mortality. The gene expression signatures may reveal why some survivors deteriorate — and how to save them.
plos-pone-0356386: Starting dialysis is psychologically shattering — but resilience follows different trajectories. This multicenter study mapped psychological resilience trajectories and their baseline predictors among patients newly initiating maintenance hemodialysis. The trajectory profiles help nephrology teams spot who’ll adapt and who needs intensive support.
plos-pone-0354186: O‘ahu’s reefs are still building carbonate — a sign of resilience. This Pacific carbonate budgets approach revealed overall net positive production around the Hawaiian island. The positive budget is rare good news for coral reefs — and a baseline for tracking whether it lasts.
plos-pone-0355686: Ethiopian children’s developmental delays go undetected — and nobody fully knew why. This descriptive qualitative study asked why implementing and accessing child developmental assessment in routine healthcare is so difficult. The findings expose the systemic barriers keeping Ethiopian children from early intervention.
plos-pone-0355286: Growing bone from stem cells — osteogenic differentiation — could heal fractures that won’t mend. This paper induced it in mesenchymal stem cells by knocking down GSK3β via siRNA transfection. The gene-silencing approach offers a precise molecular switch for turning stem cells into bone builders.
plos-pone-0350986: Soil erosion in Ethiopia’s Wolaita zone threatens livelihoods — and needs mapping. This paper spatially assessed erosion using GIS-integrated RUSLE modeling. The erosion maps pinpoint where conservation will save the most soil — directing scarce resources to the hillsides that need them most.
plos-pone-0355386: Merging onto freeways — mandatory lane changes — is a game of risk and nerve. This paper modeled the behavior with a risk appetite-enhanced game-theoretic approach for freeway merging areas. The findings could make autonomous vehicles merge the way confident — but not reckless — humans do.
plos-pone-0355186: Doctoral students using generative AI — does it help or hinder their innovative thinking? This paper explored the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ innovation behavior in the AI age through a self-determination lens. The findings reveal when AI amplifies scholarly creativity and when it hollows it out.
plos-pone-0352586: Haze obscures images — and AI can clear the air. DMSH-Net is a depth-aware multi-scale hybrid vision network for image dehazing. The architecture restores visibility in fog, smog, and haze — with applications from autonomous driving to satellite imaging.
plos-pone-0355486: 2-methoxyestradiol — an estrogen metabolite — might fight lung squamous cell carcinoma. This paper showed its effectiveness in 2D and 3D models of NCI-H2170 cells. The findings — in both flat cultures and tumor-like spheroids — nominate a hormonal compound as an unexpected cancer weapon.
plos-pone-0341786: ‘Us and them’ — dentists’ sense of division from the health system shapes whether they serve public patients. This realist interview study explored how and why system factors influence dentists’ participation in state-funded contracted primary dental care. The findings expose the trust fractures keeping dentists out of public service.
plos-pone-0354886: Blood type — ABO and Rh — might associate with macular degeneration subtypes. This cross-sectional study tested that association. The findings probe whether the antigens on red blood cells hint at risk for the eye disease stealing central vision from millions.
plos-pone-0354086: L-band pulsed radar — needing kilowatt-class power combining — got a planar four-way Gysel combiner. This paper designed it with power-aware impedance optimization. The engineering advance packs serious radar power into planar form — for defense and weather sensing alike.
plos-pone-0354386: Volcanic eruptions — disturbing the ionosphere’s total electron content — analyzed and predicted. This hybrid ML-DL model studied six eruptions against AR/MLR baselines. The findings advance space weather forecasting — because volcanoes shake the sky as well as the earth.
plos-pone-0353786: Canadian pharmacists managing anticoagulation around procedures — their role explored qualitatively. This study protocol outlines it. The planned research will map pharmacists’ periprocedural contributions. The findings promise to formalize the expertise preventing clots and bleeds — pharmacy at the procedural bedside.
plos-pone-0353486: Ankylosing spondylitis disease activity — predicted from patient-reported outcomes by machine learning. This paper built those models. The algorithms turned questionnaires into forecasts. The findings empowered patients — their own reports predicting flares before they strike.
plos-pone-0352186: Staphylococcus aureus and E. coli bloodstream infections — seasonal and heat wave incidence patterns. This prospective multicenter biometeorology study tracked them. The findings linked weather to bacteremia. The research forecasted infections — climate as the epidemiologist’s new variable.
plos-pone-0352986: Abuja’s HPV vaccine disruptions — mitigated through social media. This paper showed how. The findings demonstrated digital outreach sustaining vaccination. The research offered the playbook — social platforms as public health infrastructure. The Abuja focus is practical: Nigeria’s capital saw HPV services collapse during COVID-19, and social media offered the fastest rebuild.
plos-pone-0353186: Children with osteogenesis imperfecta — fascia iliaca compartment block for surgical analgesia in a retrospective cohort. This paper studied it. The regional block spared fragile children systemic opioids. Its value is pain control without the risks. The work eases surgery for the brittle-boned.
plos-pone-0351086: Dehumanization in faces — attractiveness and perceived intelligence differentially predicting it across race and gender intersections. This paper studied it. The findings exposed beauty and brains as dehumanization’s levers. Its social warning is stark. The work shows whose humanity the eye discounts.
plos-pone-0352386: World aquatics masters championships — performance patterns and records, with the most represented nations among top-ten swimmers. This paper analyzed them. The analysis mapped aging athletic excellence. Its sports value is the longevity. The work clocks the masters’ enduring speed.
plos-pone-0350386: Small animal CT contrast agents — iodinated, nanoparticle-based, and gadolinium-based, comparatively evaluated. This paper did so. The analysis weighed the three chemistries. Its imaging value is the choice. The work contrasts the contrasts. The three-way comparison is the practicality: it gives small-animal imagers the evidence to choose among the available chemistries.
plos-pone-0352686: Rhodococcus-infecting bacteriophages — genomic diversity characterized. This paper did so. The analysis catalogued the viruses of the industrial bacterium. Its microbiology value is the diversity. The work sequences the phages of Rhodococcus. The Rhodococcus host is the industrial angle: these bacteria degrade pollutants, and their phages shape that ability.
plos-pone-0351986: Titanium alloy Ti6Al4V ultrasonic rolling — residual stress optimized analytically. This paper developed the method. The analysis tuned the rolling for the ideal stress. Its materials value is the optimization. The work rolls the titanium to the right tension. The analytical method is the speed: it optimizes the rolling without the expense of trial-and-error experiments.
plos-pone-0351886: MNS cardiac rehabilitation teaching — a clinical practice teaching system via Delphi consensus. This paper built it. The experts converged on the teaching framework. Its education value is the agreement. The work standardizes how rehab is taught. The Delphi consensus is the method: it iterates expert opinion until the teaching framework converges.
plos-pone-0349886: Personalized inertial parameters — estimated from body hulls to musculoskeletal models. This paper developed the method. The analysis derived the body’s mass properties from its outer shape. The finding personalizes the biomechanical model. The work weighs your limbs from your silhouette.
europmc-pmc2805686: Simply teaching people about their condition can ease depression and anxiety. This 2009 meta-analysis pools trials of psychoeducation, structured information about mental illness, for depression, anxiety, and psychological distress. The authors find the approach genuinely reduces symptoms. The review backs a low-cost treatment that clinics can offer alongside therapy and medication.
europmc-pmc2824086: Rapamycin extends lifespan in many species, and this 2010 paper asks how it works in fruit flies. The authors dissect the mechanisms of life span extension by rapamycin in Drosophila melanogaster. They trace the drug's effects through the fly's biology. The mechanistic detail helped explain one of the most robust longevity interventions known.
europmc-pmc2835886: The same cell rust that wounds can be aimed at tumors. This 2010 review weighs redox control in cancer as a blade that cuts both ways, with healing promise. The authors sift how tipping oxidation might treat disease. Their take maps the lure and risk of drugging tumor chemistry.
europmc-pmc2866686: The nonstick chemical PFOA is in most blood, and this 2010 study links it to thyroid trouble. The authors tie serum PFOA levels to thyroid disease in the U.S. national health survey. Their link held across the population. The finding added the thyroid to PFOA's list of suspects.
europmc-pmc2871786: Gut bugs shift with age, and this 2010 paper follows them into extreme old age. The authors compare gut microbiota and inflammation in seniors and centenarians. Their work finds the oldest old host distinct communities. The study linked gut balance to healthy aging.
europmc-pmc2891586: Proteins work in webs, and reading those webs takes method. This 2010 review covers the essentials of protein-protein interactions, from key concepts to building and analyzing interactome networks. The authors' primer equips newcomers. Their guide opened network biology to bench scientists.
europmc-pmc2915986: Blocking two growth pathways at once can corner pancreatic cancer. This 2010 paper shows inhibiting PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK pathways wakes the FOXO factor, forcing cell cycle arrest and death in pancreatic cancer. The authors' combo strikes a lethal blow. Their work suggests a two-pronged attack.
europmc-pmc2938586: Solving protein structures needs proteins first, in bulk. This 2010 paper describes high-throughput production of human proteins for crystallization, drawn from the SGC's experience. The authors share hard-won lessons from the pipeline. Their methods fed the structural genomics boom. Many labs copied their recipes.
europmc-pmc2949686: The actin gene family builds the cell's skeleton in many flavors. This 2010 review argues function follows isoform across actin variants. The authors' synthesis clarifies a crowded field. Their review guides cytoskeleton research. Drug hunters targeting cell shape read it closely.
europmc-pmc2952586: A protein tied to ALS gathers in stress granules. This 2010 paper shows TDP-43 associates with stress granules in cultured cells and diseased brain tissue. The authors' microscopy reveals the clumping in detail. Their work links stress biology to neurodegeneration. The clumps may seed the disease's spread.
europmc-pmc2996186: Water carries bacterial killers, and this 2010 review lists them. The author covers the germs that ride drinking and pool water. Their overview informs water safety rules. The review aids public health teams. Cholera and typhoid top the danger list. Boiling remains the surest defense.
europmc-pmc3017786: Soybeans got a gene activity atlas. This 2010 paper maps which soybean genes switch on in each tissue. The authors' atlas aids crop science. Their resource supports smarter breeding. Oil and protein traits top the wish list. Breeders query the atlas before each cross.
europmc-pmc3104486: Gene activity got truly measured. This 2011 paper pits microarrays against deep sequencing for reading the transcriptome. The authors show sequencing wins on every front. Their work pushed RNA-seq mainstream. Labs retired their arrays. The paper is a methods classic.
europmc-pmc3168486: Blood amino acids flagged five cancers. This 2011 paper profiles plasma amino acids in five cancer types for early detection. The authors reveal the patterns. Their work points to screening tests. The profiles caught cancers early, they found. A commercial test followed the work.
europmc-pmc3170586: Pregnancy immune signals tied to autism. This 2011 study finds higher mid-pregnancy cytokines in mothers of autistic children. The authors reveal the link. Their work guides research. The signals appeared months before birth. The finding needs replication, they caution. It opened the maternal-immune hypothesis.
europmc-pmc3238286: Gene network modules got a concepts guide. This 2007 paper explains network ideas behind gene modules. The authors clarify the concepts. Their work trained biologists. WGCNA grew from these ideas. The tutorial is widely taught. Horvath's lab led the work. The guide remains widely used.
europmc-pmc3334586: Anatomy got a shared dictionary. This 2012 paper brings Uberon, a cross-species anatomy standard. The authors build the dictionary. Their work underpins databases. Mungall's team led the work. The standard is open access. Databases adopted it widely. It is widely cited.
europmc-pmc3459986: Two genes got a non-enzyme role. This 2012 paper shows UTX and UTY work without their enzyme function in mice. The authors reveal the role. Their work guides genetics. Shpargel's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It is a classic.
europmc-pmc6521386: Bile acids help digest fat, but gut bacteria chemically remodel them into secondary forms that shape gut health. Using computer models of microbial metabolism, researchers mapped which gut species can perform each transformation step. The work reveals distinct metabolic talents across microbes - and flags which bacterial capabilities go missing in inflammatory bowel disease, where bile-acid balance breaks down.
europmc-pmc6559986: In glioblastoma - the deadliest brain tumor - reactive astrocytes switch sides, helping the cancer hide. This study shows tumor-associated astrocytes rewire their genes to build an immunosuppressive cocoon around the tumor, shielding it from attack. Cracking that crosstalk could expose brain tumors to the immune system.
europmc-pmc6565686: The blood-brain barrier blocks most drugs from entering the brain - testing which ones slip through needs a realistic model. Researchers built a BBB on a chip: human stem-cell-derived vessel cells in a microfluidic device, matured under low oxygen to mimic the real barrier. The chip correctly predicted how drugs and antibodies cross, offering a lab stand-in for human brains.
europmc-pmc6595586: Everyone walks at their own pace - and pace changes everything about how we move. This systematic review and meta-analysis pulled together studies on how walking speed reshapes gait mechanics in healthy people. The results give clinicians a baseline: without accounting for speed, you cannot tell normal variation from real walking problems.
europmc-pmc6636886: Health campaigns use behavior-change tricks - but which tricks work through which mental levers? This synthesis maps published links between behavior change techniques and their mechanisms of action. The result is a Rosetta Stone for intervention designers: pick a technique, see the lever it pulls.
europmc-pmc6734286: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals tissues cell by cell - but naming each cell is tedious manual labor. This study compared automatic cell-identification methods head to head on real datasets. The benchmark tells researchers which tools to trust when the cell census numbers in the millions.
europmc-pmc6743286: Radiation aimed at chest tumors can scar the lungs it passes through. This review covers radiation-induced lung injury: the early inflammation (pneumonitis) and the late stiffening (fibrosis) that cap how much radiation doctors can deliver. Protecting lungs means treating more tumor.
europmc-pmc6755986: Can eating well ward off depression? Pooling observational studies, this review tested whether healthy dietary patterns link to lower depression risk. The answer leans yes: better diets track with better moods. Nutrition, the findings suggest, belongs in the mental-health toolkit.
europmc-pmc6764986: Lab workhorse tags for proteins are often one-trick ponies. The ALFA-tag is a rationally designed epitope tag built for versatility: detecting, purifying, and imaging proteins across many applications. The tiny tag punches above its weight in the nanobody toolkit.
europmc-pmc6784786: Fatty liver can smolder for years - or march toward cirrhosis. Following biopsies over time, this study tied microscopic disease activity to whether nonalcoholic fatty liver disease progresses or retreats. The histology forecast helps doctors know which livers need watching.
europmc-pmc6784886: Dengue now threatens over half of humanity - and its range keeps growing. This study mapped the mosquito-borne virus's current and future global distribution, factoring in climate and urbanization. The risk maps show where the next half-billion at-risk people live.
europmc-pmc6833286: Sepsis is the immune system at war with itself - and the war litter matters. This review covers DAMPs and NETs: the alarm cries and white-cell traps that feed sepsis inflammation. The tiny ruins are a therapy target. Calm the litter, calm the storm.
europmc-pmc6889286: A long RNA shields lung tumors from iron death. This study found LINC00336 inhibits ferroptosis in lung cancer by acting as a competing endogenous RNA - sponging the microRNAs that would kill. The shield is a drug target. Break the shield, and the tumor rusts.
europmc-pmc6906186: Mouse cures keep flopping in humans - lab-grown brain cells offer hope. This review maps copying Alzheimer's illness with iPSC-derived brain cells: human nerve cells in a dish. The models bring drug trials closer to people. Real cells, human answers. The dish beats the mouse for carryover.
europmc-pmc6946686: A cut-and-paste player doubles in cancer spread. This study found U1 snRNP steers cancer cell crawling and breaching in dish. The RNA machine's dark side. Stubby mRNA tails free the roamers. Near tail-adding cues drive the switch. The most plentiful snRNP takes on new jobs.
europmc-pmc6966486: Defense cells reroute fat burning to fight or heal. This review maps fat fuel use in the fuel rewiring of guard cells: M1 versus M2 fuel choices. The guard cell fuel menu. Sugar-burning versus fat burning, charted. Diet and drugs could guide guard cell doom.
europmc-pmc6969186: Light-activated nano-enzymes turn growth oxygen against itself. This study built a self-built one-atom nano-enzyme for boosted light care of growths. The low-air-proof light care. Dense growth low air limits standard PDT. OxgeMCC-r supplies its own oxygen. Killer oxygen, made on demand. A safe, handy nano-agent for deep growths.
europmc-pmc6978386: Skin cancer ducks iron death via a protein tag machine. This study found Nedd4 tags VDAC2/3 to muzzle erastin-induced ferroptosis in skin cancer. The exit door, found. Erastin latches pore proteins but defiance pops up. Jamming Nedd4 brings back ferroptosis weakness. A new lever against skin cancer drug defiance.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1186: The full 2007 Government Accountability Office report on U.S. programs helping other countries build disease-surveillance capacity — companion to GAO's testimony on the same subject. It details how American agencies funded labs, training, and reporting systems abroad to catch outbreaks early. The report evaluates whether those investments were creating a genuinely stronger global warning network.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-986: The drug-benefit rollout's money got a clean-ish bill from GAO in 2007 — spending rules were in place for the new Medicare drug program, though some lapses showed. The findings credit the Social Security Administration's bookkeeping while flagging the cracks. Big new benefit, mostly steady hands on the purse.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-786: The Congressional Award's books got an audit in 2007 — GAO's report grades the youth foundation's finances for 2006 and 2005. The findings deliver the formal audit opinion in full. The report shows the watchdog's reach: even Congress's own charities get the once-over.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-486: American aid was saving mothers and babies abroad in 2007 — GAO's report says the programs reached far and wide, but the spending details stayed fuzzy. The findings praise the reach and prod the books. The report's standard is fair: good deeds deserve good accounting.
gao-gaoreports-b-299086: Synectic Solutions took its February 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Every challenger gets the full fair-play hearing.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-86: Surgery-center payments needed a fairer formula in 2007, and GAO's report says Medicare should tie them to the hospital outpatient system. The findings make the case. The report warns that the same procedure should not cost double by address. The price had to be consistent.
gao-gaoreports-b-298086: Bristol Group doubled its May 2006 protest — two case numbers, one Union Station venture — and GAO's combined ruling settles both. The firm challenged the awards, and the call weighs each claim. Paired filings get one careful answer. Two dockets, one fair verdict.
gao-gaoreports-b-297986: Knowledge Connections took its May 2006 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Every challenger gets the full fair-play hearing.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-386: The bank secrecy framework needed strengthening in 2006, and GAO's report says opportunities existed for FinCEN and regulators to improve it. The findings target the gaps. The report warns that the money-laundering net needed tighter mesh. The framework had to be strengthened.
gao-gaoreports-b-297686: CRAssociates took its March 2006 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Every challenger gets the full fair-play hearing. The process stays the same for all.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-86: The SEC's people management was improving in 2006, and GAO's report says some progress had been made on human capital strategy. The findings give the partial credit. The report warns that the market watchdog's workforce needed tending. The progress had to continue.
gao-gaoreports-gao-05-686: Exon-Florio's implementation needed strengthening in 2005, and GAO's report says enhancements could improve the law's effectiveness. The findings demand the upgrades. The report warns that the foreign-deal reviews deserved teeth. The implementation had to be stronger. The foreign-deal reviews deserved teeth.
gao-gaoreports-gao-05-986: Corporate tech chiefs' roles got a GAO review in 2005, and the report examines responsibilities and governance at leading companies. The findings take the measure. The report shows the private-sector CIOs were studied. The roles had to be understood. The private-sector CIOs were studied.
openalex-w7204858686: After the Rio Doce mining disaster, a teacher-training course asked educators to turn the tragedy into lessons. This article studies a teaching product built in that course at a public school in Caratinga, Minas Gerais, and what the training added to teaching about mining. The authors assess how the experience shaped classroom practice. Education as repair work in a community still living with the damage.
arxiv-2606-16086: Forecasters mix live readings with physics code to call the weather. This paper runs a lean Kalman filter — a classic guess-tuner — on simple flow math, using dice-roll traits to keep sums cheap. It is for math pros who fuse sensor feeds into earth models.
arxiv-2606-16286: Robots learn movement policies from demonstrations, and "flow matching" is a popular way to train them — but the policies can be jerky or unsafe. FlowMPC improves flow-matching policies by combining them with world models that predict what will happen, adding model-predictive control. It targets robotics researchers building smoother, safer learned controllers.
arxiv-2606-16386: Coordinating drone swarms at low altitude — dodging buildings, each other, and no-fly zones — is a multi-agent nightmare. This paper applies game-theoretic multi-agent reinforcement learning to plan swarm trajectories, treating each drone as a player in a game. It targets robotics researchers building safe autonomous fleets.
arxiv-2606-16586: Multimodal language models often miss fine details in images — a small defect, a subtle difference. LOCUS improves fine-grained perception by searching for the most informative local visual cues before answering. The paper targets AI researchers making vision-language models notice what matters in high-detail images.
arxiv-2606-16686: Neutrinos have inexplicably tiny masses, and dark matter's identity is unknown — perhaps one framework explains both. This paper proposes a minimal "dark U(1)" model with an inverse seesaw mechanism for neutrino masses plus a dark matter candidate. It targets particle theorists unifying the two biggest mysteries.
arxiv-2606-16786: AI explanation tools claim to show why a model decided — but connecting those tools to real-world needs is messy. This paper argues we need 'explanation cards': standard summaries linking each explanation algorithm to its real use. It is for explainable-AI researchers bridging lab and practice.
arxiv-2606-16886: Checking software correctness with pure logic is powerful but slow; local language models are fast but sloppy. This paper hyper-charges local LLMs with symbolic reasoning for software verification: fast guesses, checked by logic. It is for formal-methods researchers. Speed plus proof.
